description.value: The study assessed fMRI responses to food, cocaine, and neutral visual cues presented subliminally or supraliminally, and examined whether cue reactivity varied by time of day.

spans.text: Here we assessed functional MRI (fMRI) responses to food, cocaine, and neutral cues presented at a subliminal ("unconscious", 33 ms) and supraliminal ("conscious", 750 and 3000 ms) level in healthy, cocaine naïve volunteers.
Because there is evidence of circadian variability in reward sensitivity, our second aim was to assess diurnal variability in the brain's reactivity to cues.

design.value: A repeated-measures event-related fMRI study in which 16 healthy cocaine-naïve volunteers completed three cue-presentation sessions twice, once in the morning and once in the evening, with food, cocaine, and neutral images presented for 33, 750, or 3000 ms.

spans.text: Sixteen participants completed two randomly ordered fMRI sessions (once 9-11 AM and another 5-7 PM). in which food, cocaine, and neutral cues were presented for 33, 750 and 3000 ms.
A total of 40 appetitive food, 40 cocaine-related and 40 neutral images were presented in a randomized order in an event-related design using E-prime software.
Neutral pictures included neutral items from the International Affective Picture System (IAPS) (Lang et al. 2008) and from in-house pictures libraries (Childress et al. 2008; Volkow et al. 2006).
